newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Ford expects Asia sales to double in 4-5 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Ford expects Asia sales to double in 4-5 yrs.

text.p: Ford Motor Co expects its sales in Asia to more than double within the next four to five years, Kenneth Brown, director of Asian markets public affairs said on Monday.
Speaking to reporters at a briefing, Brown said Ford sold 320,000 vehicles in the Asia Pacific (including Japan, Australia and New Zealand) in 1995.
This constituted about 2.4 percent of a total of 13.5 million vehicles sold in the region in 1995.
"From a two percent player, we expect to become a five percent player in the next four to five years...most of the increase should come from India and China," he said.
Brown also dismissed recent concerns about a growing glut of motor production capacity in Asia.
He said the glut in capacity was mostly in mature markets like Japan and South Korea. "Outside those areas, the excess capacity is not terribly high."
He said that in Thailand there was capacity for 900,000 units against domestic sales of 588,000 units last year.
After taking into account some exports, Thailand's excess capacity could be in the region of 100,000-200,000 units which should be used up in a couple of years, he said.
Brown, who is based in Thailand, also said the economic slowdown in the country had affected motor sales which is currently down about 15 percent year-on-year.
Ford, which sold 4,520 vehicles in Thailand last year, expects to be similarly affected though the decline should be less than 15 percent.
Brown said Ford's plans to get new dealers and to introduce new products in Thailand should underpine sales there.
"We have not altered any long-term plans in Thailand and our factory is going ahead. There is still a lot of growth in the motor industry in Thailand, especially outside the Bangkok area," he said.
The U.S. auto company has a US$500 million joint venture to start a pickup truck manufacturing facility in Thailand by May 1998.
Elsewhere in the region, the company expects to start production of trucks in Vietnam by October 1997 and is also conducting feasibility studies for a production facility in the Philippines.
It is also developing a light commercial vehicle in China with its joint venture partner Jiangling Motors Corp.
